subject: Transportation Systems
title: Fuselage Structure
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fuselage Structure.

hook.text: At 35,000 feet, the air outside would kill you in seconds. The fuselage is your pressurized bubble.

buildup.text: The cabin is pumped to the equivalent of 6,000 feet altitude. Your body barely notices the difference.

discovery.text: This pressure difference puts enormous stress on the fuselage—like inflating a balloon from inside.

twist.text: Every landing depressurizes and every takeoff re-pressurizes. Over years, this cycling fatigues the metal.

climax.text: Engineers inspect fuselages for microscopic cracks. One missed crack can become a catastrophe.

punchline.text: The cabin is a balloon that inflates 30,000 times.

quiz.question: Why does pressurization stress the fuselage?
options: Pressure inside is higher than outside, expanding the hull
